High-temperature exposure produces extensive surface deposition together with aligned linear features and triangular faceted surface features. …

articles.authors: Leonid Arantchouk, Thomas Clark, Magali Lozano, Aurelien Houard
articles.summary: We study the development of laser-guided, meter-scale electric discharges produced in air by a Tesla AC voltage generator. Using ultrafast imaging, we observe the propagation of streamers produced in the presence of femtosecond laser filaments when a 100 μs oscillatory voltage of 300 kV is applied to a rod electrode. We found that the streamers propagate much faster in the low-density gas channel formed by the filament when the voltage polarity is negative. Their propagation is unaffected by a grounded second electrode at the filament's end. …

articles.summary: Femtosecond laser grooving is used as a pre-processing step ahead of the mechanical dicing of low-k dielectrics, which are brittle and prone to cracking and delamination under stress. To relate the groove geometry and the debris height to the processing parameters, SiCOH low-k wafers were grooved at a fixed pulse duration of 250 fs under an infrared condition at 1030 nm and an ultraviolet condition at 343 nm, with nominal spot diameters of 12 and 7 µm, respectively. Each groove was formed in eight passes. …

articles.summary: This study explores the amorphization of a Te-poor Ge–Sb–Te alloy using single 800 nm femtosecond laser pulses. Before irradiation, the phase composition and microstructure of the investigated sample were characterized using synchrotron x-ray diffraction and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. The threshold fluence required for amorphization with a single laser shot was identified, with a minimum fluence of ∼45 mJ cm−2 necessary to induce structural changes. At higher fluences (≥83 mJ cm−2), surface blistering and layer delamination occurred, also due to laser absorption by the TiN capping layer. …

articles.summary: Two-photon lithography (2PL) is a microfabrication technique that has become a standard method for the generation of miniaturized 3D objects. A promising novel approach to laser direct writing is two-photon cross-linking (2PC), which uses thin solid films of copolymers containing small amounts of chromophores acting as a two-photon cross-linker. Upon activation by two-photon light absorption, they form polymer networks through cross-linking via C–H insertion (CHic) at the focal point of the laser beam. As the focal volume moves, polymer structures are written into the film as a latent image. …

articles.summary: Flexible strain sensors are essential components of wearable electronic devices. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity, stable electrical conductivity, a wide working strain range, and controllable structural fabrication remains a major challenge. In this study, a laser-induced graphene/multi-walled carbon nanotube (LIG/MWCNTs) composite conductive network regulated by fingerprint-inspired microcracks was fabricated through laser direct writing. …

articles.title: Coexistence of dipolar and quadrupolar higher-order topology
articles.authors: Konstantin Rodionenko, Maxim Mazanov, Maxim A. Gorlach
articles.summary: Two-dimensional higher-order topological insulators are typically classified either as dipolar or quadrupolar depending on the relevant invariant. These two classes were previously considered non-overlapping. Here we put forward an example system exhibiting dipolar and quadrupolar higher-order topology simultaneously, suggest its implementation using the arrays of laser-written evanescently coupled optical waveguides and support our conclusions by the full-wave numerical simulations.

articles.authors: Dominik Mücke, Cemal Esen, Ralf Hellmann
articles.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
articles.summary: We report on deep laser ablation of fused silica using ultrashort pulses at a high pulse frequency rate of 1000 kHz, enabling highly precise and fast generation of 2.5D structures, such as, e.g., optical elements and microfluidic elements. Depending on the specific demands of such applications in terms of surface roughness and geometrical features, initially the applied fluence is finely chosen in conjunction with the scan velocity and a fine refocusing to ablate defined layer heights even across larger ablation depths. Specifically, our approach allows a consistent layer-wise ablation of 1 µm down to at least 1900 µm with an error of below 0.5 % with respect to the targeted depth. …

articles.authors: Jiaqing Pei, Kai Yin, Lingxiao Wang, Xinghao Song, Jianqiang Xiao, Hao Song, Yuchun He
articles.summary: Crude oil becomes highly viscous and may solidify at low temperatures, reducing pipeline throughput and increasing transport energy demand. Conventional heating systems require complex infrastructure and substantial energy input, limiting their use in low‐energy, high‐performance oil transport. Here, we report a flash femtosecond laser route that creates an in situ photothermal superhydrophobic high‐entropy alloy nanoparticle (HEA‐NPs)/aluminum surface for solar‐assisted crude oil transport. The transient heating and quenching generated by the laser produce FeCoNiCrMnLa HEA‐NPs and distribute them uniformly across the hierarchical aluminum substrate (HEAs/PA). …

articles.title: Boosting bottom-up milling of glass with GHz laser bursts
articles.authors: Miglė Mackevičiūtė, Juozas Dudutis, Aleksandras Kondratas, Paulius Gečys
articles.summary: Burst-mode laser processing has gained increasing attention in material machining due to its potential to enhance processing efficiency and quality. However, most studies have focused on conventional top-down machining strategies, while investigations of bottom-up milling (BUM) remain limited. In this work, we optimize processing parameters for high-efficiency glass milling using a bottom-up approach with GHz bursts. The results show that the highest BUM efficiencies are achieved when employing high pulse counts (\geq 20). To the best of our knowledge, we report the highest glass milling efficiency, reaching more than 250 μm3/μJ for both soda-lime glass and fused silica. …

articles.summary: In‐sensor information processing and image encryption transmission are critical for next‐generation optoelectronic devices with low data latency and robust information security. However, unidirectional photoresponse and complex architectures hinder the integration of optical information processing and image encryption transmission. Here, we design a two‐terminal photodetector based on a Te/MoS 2 /WSe 2 heterojunction, exhibiting excellent broadband self‐powered photodetection with the responsivity, shot‐noise‐limited specific detectivity, and external quantum efficiency of 310.3 mA/W, 3.79 × 10 12 Jones, and 94.9%, respectively. …

articles.summary: This work investigates the sensing capabilities of a compact, all-in-fibre Mach–Zehnder interferometer (MZI) fabricated using femtosecond laser inscription. The device was created within the cladding region of a single-mode optical fibre, in close proximity to the cladding–air interface, enabling light extraction from the core and enhanced evanescent-field interaction with the surrounding environment. The sensing structure integrates three collocated optical elements: a cladding-based MZI, a fibre Bragg grating (FBG) inscribed within the MZI sensing arm, and a conventional FBG inscribed in the fibre core, providing distinct and complementary sensing responses. …

articles.authors: Gongxin Li, Yuting Mao, Fei Liu, fangmei an, Qiang Zhan
articles.summary: As minimally invasive surgery (MIS) ventures into increasingly confined and delicate anatomical regions, conventional tethered instruments encounter inherent limitations in miniaturization and maneuverability. Untethered magnetic microrobots, characterized by precise navigation, deep tissue penetration, and highly efficient propulsion in low-Reynolds-number fluids, have emerged as a transformative platform for targeted diagnostics and therapeutics with sub-millimeter accuracy. This review systematically examines the state-of-the-art breakthroughs and the clinical translation landscape of magnetic microrobotic systems. …

While conventional instruments provide precise single point measurements, their rigidity and weight limit deployment on emerging platforms that could extend observational reach. Here, we introduce the fully integrated, flexible temperature–depth sensor deployable on curved and mobile surfaces for deep-sea measurements. …

articles.authors: Entesar A. Ganash, Salihah A. Al-zahrani, Hala A. Al-Jawhari, Reem M. Altuwirqi
articles.summary: The increasing global water scarcity, driven by population growth, industrialization, and climate change, has created an urgent need for sustainable and efficient water desalination. This study focuses on developing a solar-driven steam generation (SSG) desalination system that uses photothermal materials (PTMs), such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and graphene produced via laser-induced graphene (LIG), to enhance evaporation efficiency. The system was prepared by coating melamine foam (MF), used as the base, with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) at varying concentrations (0.6 wt%–1.4 wt%), with the 1 wt% concentration showing the highest evaporation rate. …

articles.authors: Alina Karabchevsky, Shadad Watad, Aviad Katiyi, Muhammad Sharif Uddin, Nicolás Abadía, Anupma Thakur, Babak Anasori
articles.summary: MXenes - a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides - have emerged as powerful nonlinear photonic materials owing to their metallic conductivity, ultrafast carrier dynamics, broadband optical response, and highly tunable surface chemistry. This Review provides the first comprehensive overview of the nonlinear optical (NLO) properties of MXenes and their growing impact on advanced photonic technologies. We discuss state-of-the-art synthesis strategies, from fluoride-based etching to molten-salt, electrochemical, and CVD-enabled routes, highlighting how structural quality and surface terminations govern optical behaviour. …

articles.summary: The paper systematizes modern approaches to the classification, formation, and industrial application of micro-optical structures. The main directions of their use in image formation and optical radiation control systems, information photonics, sensors, biophotonics, lighting engineering, and optical identification tools are considered. A multi-level classification of micro-optical elements is proposed based on their functional purpose, the type of optical field transformation, geometric complexity, and spatial organization. …

articles.authors: Mobin Yaghoobi, Seyedeh Mahshad Hosseini, Leila Hajshahvaladi, Gholam-Mohammad Parsanasab, Mohammad Ismail Zibaii
articles.summary: Whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microlasers are promising for refractometric sensing, but their practical implementation can be limited by the need for stable resonator-coupler alignment. Here, we demonstrate a Rhodamine B-doped polymer WGM microring laser directly fabricated on an optical-fiber tip, eliminating the external resonator-fiber coupling interface at the sensing head. Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined for fabrication, while finite-difference time-domain simulations guide the microring laser design. The microlasers operate in air and water with thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively. …

A radial–azimuthal polarization converter placed in the probe beam produces a doughnut-shaped beam whose local polarization varies continuously with azimuthal angle, thereby encoding the full range of linear polarization orientations from 0 to 2π within a single transverse beam profile. …

articles.title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation
articles.authors: Renjie Li, Yuanhao Zhou, Yinqi Zeng, Edward Lukhanin, Huan Liu, Carter McNear, Daniel Ceballos, Mohamed Eshan, Olamide Ogunjobi, Owen Funke, Yu Liu, Yuxing Wang, Gregory Victor Lowry, Paul J. Braun, Lynford L. Goddard
articles.summary: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the laboratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a self-evolving laboratory framework that connects computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs. These changes are retained as reusable skills and infrastructure, allowing the laboratory to develop alongside its scientific tasks. …

articles.authors: Robert Stuckert, Felix Pohl, Oleg Prymak, Nikola Apanowicz, Christoph Rehbock, Ulrich Schürmann, Michael Farle, Dierk Raabe, Lorenz Kienle, Stephan Barcikowski, Natalia Shkodich
articles.summary: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) offer compositional and structural tunability for applications, like water splitting, H2O2 production, or magnetocaloric technologies. Therefore, the interplay between composition, structure, and functionality is of significant interest for materials´ functionality optimization. Microparticle laser fragmentation in liquid flow (MP-LFL) is an emerging scalable method for nanoalloy production, but remains underexplored for HEA NPs. Here, we investigate CrFeCoNiX (X = Ga, Cu, Mo) HEA NPs fabricated by MP-LFL in ethanol and examine how compositional variations affect elemental homogeneity, size, phase structure, and magnetic properties. …
